scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that the modern world is more complex, then argues the past still guides us; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Each generation likes to believe its problems are entirely new and unlike any before.
One claim holds that knowing about the past cannot help us make decisions today, on the reason that the modern world is far more complex than it once was.
I disagree with the claim, because the past still teaches lessons that help us even in a complex world.

sections.role: Body 1 — The truth that the world is more complex

sentences.text: First, there is some truth in the reason that today's world is more complex.
Modern life involves global trade, advanced technology, and problems that earlier ages never faced.
For example, no ancient ruler ever had to manage the internet or worldwide climate change.
This shows that the past cannot offer a ready answer to every modern problem.
Old solutions, copied blindly, may not fit a far more complicated present.
Each new age clearly brings challenges that demand fresh and original thinking.
To this extent, the reason is not entirely without merit.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why the past still helps

sentences.text: Second, however, the claim that the past cannot help us today is plainly false.
Human nature and many basic problems have stayed remarkably the same across the centuries.
Consider how the study of past financial crashes still helps leaders avoid the same mistakes.
Such lessons show that history offers real guidance even in a complex modern world.
Greater complexity is a reason to study the past more carefully, not to ignore it.
Ignoring history would force us to relearn painful lessons that earlier people already mastered.
The past, then, remains a valuable guide despite the complexity of the present.
In conclusion, the modern world is indeed more complex than the world of the past.
But this makes the lessons of history more useful, not less, in guiding our decisions.
We decide most wisely today by learning from the past while adapting it to a complex present.
